title: Consumer Protection Act 2019
text: Consumer means any person who buys any goods for a consideration which has been paid or promised or partly paid and partly promised, or under any system of deferred payment, and includes any user of such goods other than the person who buys such goods for consideration paid or promised or partly paid or partly promised, or under any system of deferred payment, when such use is made with the approval of such person, but does not include a person who obtains such goods for resale or for any commercial purpose.
limitations: Excerpt only; statutory exceptions and the complete definition must be checked in the official Act.

title: Consumer Protection Act 2019
text: A complaint, in relation to any goods sold or delivered or agreed to be sold or delivered or any service provided or agreed to be provided, may be filed with a District Commission by the consumer to whom such goods are sold or delivered or agreed to be sold or delivered or such service is provided or agreed to be provided; or any recognised consumer association; or one or more consumers, where there are numerous consumers having the same interest; or the Central Government, Central Authority or State Government.
limitations: Excerpt omits conditions and later subsections; consult the complete current Act and rules.

title: Consumer Protection Act 2019
text: Where the District Commission is satisfied that the goods complained against suffer from any of the defects specified in the complaint or that any of the allegations contained in the complaint about the services or any unfair trade practices are proved, it may issue an order to remove the defect, replace the goods with new goods of similar description which shall be free from any defect, or return to the complainant the price or charges paid by the complainant along with such interest as may be decided.
limitations: Paraphrased excerpt of selected clauses; other remedies, proof requirements, and procedure are omitted.

title: Consumer Protection Act 2019
text: The District Commission, the State Commission or the National Commission shall not admit a complaint unless it is filed within two years from the date on which the cause of action has arisen. A complaint may be entertained after that period if the complainant satisfies the Commission that there was sufficient cause for not filing within that period and the reasons for condoning delay are recorded.
limitations: Applicability to a specific case requires facts and current-law review.

title: National Consumer Helpline About
text: The National Consumer Helpline portal is a pre-litigation grievance mechanism. It forwards grievances to the concerned company, agency, regulator or ombudsman. It does not guarantee a remedy. If the grievance is not resolved to the consumer's satisfaction, the consumer may approach the appropriate Consumer Commission. The portal says the process may take up to 30 days to reach a logical conclusion.
limitations: Operational guidance can change; verify the current portal before acting.

title: National Consumer Helpline Contact Details
text: The National Consumer Helpline lists toll-free numbers 1915 and 1800 11 4000, available 8 AM to 8 PM except national holidays, and provides web, SMS, WhatsApp, app and UMANG channels for consumer grievances.
limitations: Contact details and hours may change; verify on the official page.

title: Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020
text: An e-commerce entity must maintain a grievance-redress mechanism and display the grievance officer's details. Rule 4 states that the officer must acknowledge a consumer complaint within forty-eight hours and redress it within one month from receipt.
limitations: Read with the corrigendum and later amendments, including the 2021 and 2026 amendments. Whether the rule applies depends on the seller and transaction.

title: Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020
text: For marketplace sales, Rule 6(3) addresses a seller's refusal to take back goods or refund consideration when goods or services are defective, deficient, spurious, not as advertised or agreed, or delivered late, subject to the rule's terms and the force-majeure proviso for delayed delivery.
limitations: Paraphrased selected provision. Check the complete current rule, amendments, platform model and factual conditions before applying it.

title: Consumer Commission Jurisdiction Rules, 2021
text: The 2021 Rules allocate pecuniary jurisdiction by the value paid as consideration: District Commission up to fifty lakh rupees; State Commission above fifty lakh and up to two crore rupees; National Commission above two crore rupees.
limitations: This does not decide territorial jurisdiction, maintainability, valuation disputes, appeals or whether later amendments apply.

title: Consumer Commission Procedure Regulations, 2020
text: Regulation 7 sets copy requirements for physical institution of complaints, appeals and revision petitions, including additional copies corresponding to the number of opposite parties or respondents.
limitations: Online filing through the current official platform may use a different workflow. Check current portal instructions and later amendments before filing.

title: Consumer Protection (Mediation) Rules, 2020
text: Rule 4 identifies matters that are not to be referred to mediation, including specified serious medical-negligence matters, serious and specific allegations of fraud or forgery, non-compoundable offences, and matters involving public interest or many non-parties. The Commission may also find mediation unsuitable in other circumstances.
limitations: Suitability is case-specific and the Commission controls referral. This passage is not a recommendation to mediate.

title: Department of Consumer Affairs Consumer Protection Unit
locator: Consumer Protection Unit page, last updated 15 October 2026
text: The Department of Consumer Affairs identifies e-Jagriti as the portal administered by its Consumer Protection Division for consumer-commission digital services and links to https://e-jagriti.gov.in/.
limitations: Portal screens, accepted formats, fees, service steps and availability can change. Verify the live official portal before filing.

title: NALSA FAQs on Legal Services
text: NALSA explains that legal services may include advice, representation, process expenses in appropriate cases, preparation of pleadings, drafting legal documents, and supplying certified copies. It distinguishes legal advice and assistance from representation and describes routes to legal-services institutions.
limitations: Do not promise eligibility, assignment of a lawyer or availability. Current eligibility and the appropriate institution require individual verification.

title: Experion Developers Pvt. Ltd. v. Sushma Ashok Shiroor
locator: Civil Appeal Nos. 6044 and 7149 of 2019, paragraphs 15-19
text: The Supreme Court held, on the homebuyer facts before it and under the Consumer Protection Act 1986, that the Commission had power to direct refund. The judgment states: “the Commission has the power and jurisdiction to direct return of money”.
limitations: Homebuyer dispute involving the 1986 Act and RERA. It is not direct authority for ordinary retail goods, does not guarantee a refund, and subsequent treatment was not independently checked.
